How they’re built

Two different pipelines. Pip combines three images, drawn cracks and CSS scaling. Minty uses one sprite sheet and changes position within it.

Pip 3 separate PNGs

Minty sprite sheet

PipMinty
ArtworkMicrosoft Fluent Emoji 3D (MIT). Soft gradients, no outline.Original generated art. 2D sticker style, thick plum outline, cel shading.
Filesegg.png, hatching.png, chick.png, each 256 × 256triceratops-sprite-sheet.png, …, 5 × 2 cells of …
Egg stagesOne egg image. egg-cracks.js draws thin SVG crack lines on top: 0, 2, 5, then 7 of its 9 strokes.Four painted frames, egg-0–egg-3. Cracks, glow and the frill peeking out are drawn into the art.
Hatchinghatching.png, scaled to 88%hatch frame, shown at full size
GrowthOne chick.png, scaled by CSS from 62% to 100% (--chick-scale). Grows a little on every feed.Five drawn frames, level-1–level-5 (bigger, leaf, neckerchief). Changes only at a new level.
Ground shadowCSS ellipse (.companion-ground) with fixed pixel positionsPainted into every frame. No CSS shadow.
Roster tileOnly egg.png or chick.png, never cracks or growthShows the current frame
RenderercompanionArt(): an <img> plus an optional <svg>petArt() with .atlas-frame: a CSS background with background-position in % steps. The sheet’s JSON frame map isn’t read by the app.

What doesn’t match

What the differences above mean in practice.

Directions

Three ways to make them belong together.

ONE PIPELINE · SUGGESTED

Redraw Pip as a 5 × 2 sheet in Minty’s style

  • Every companion becomes “a sheet with the same 10 frames”. Adding a third needs only art.
  • egg-cracks.js, --chick-scale and the CSS shadow go away.
  • Needs 10 new Pip frames. The Microsoft licence is then no longer needed.
  • Existing saves keep working, because frames come from progress, not files.
SAME CODE, SAME LOOK

Pack Pip’s Fluent art into a sheet

  • Unifies rendering: bake the cracks and growth sizes into 10 frames.
  • Pip still looks 3D next to a 2D Minty.
  • 256 px sources stay soft on iPhone.
KEEP PIP

Redraw Minty in the Fluent 3D style

  • Pip stays untouched.
  • Fluent has no triceratops, so it would have to be generated to match Microsoft’s style, which is hard to keep consistent.
  • Every future companion carries the same problem.

Decisions to make first

  1. Which style wins: 2D sticker (Minty) or 3D glossy (Pip)?
  2. Ground shadow: painted into each frame, or one CSS shadow shared by every companion?
  3. Growth feedback: a visible change on every feed, or only at a new level?
  4. Where the feet sit and how tall each stage is: pick targets from the Measurements table so every sheet follows them.

Try new art
